title: BitWave: Exploiting Column-Based Bit-Level Sparsity for Deep Learning Acceleration
problem: Existing bit-serial accelerators suffer from inefficient memory accesses when exploiting bit-level sparsity due to irregular indices of non-zero bits, making memory access a critical bottleneck despite computation reduction. Traditional approaches cannot efficiently handle the irregular sparsity patterns that emerge from bit-level compression.
motivation: Memory accesses dominate DNN accelerator performance, so enabling efficient memory patterns while exploiting sparsity is critical for achieving high-performance deep learning acceleration.
method: BitWave introduces a bit-column-serial computing paradigm that processes structured bit-level sparsity efficiently by organizing computation around bit columns rather than individual bits. The architecture combines dynamic dataflow techniques with redundant computation skipping and weight compression to reduce both computations and memory footprints. Post-training optimization with selected weight bit-flips avoids performance degradation and eliminates the need for model retraining.
key_novelty: The bit-column-serial approach that restructures computation to align with column-based bit organization, enabling efficient memory access patterns while exploiting bit-level sparsity.
contributions: Introduced novel bit-column-serial computing paradigm for efficient sparsity exploitation
BitWave hardware architecture achieving 13.25x speedup and 7.71x efficiency over state-of-the-art sparsity accelerators
Post-training weight bit-flip optimization technique that avoids retraining while maintaining accuracy
Compact design (1.138 mm² area, 17.56 mW power) in 16nm FinFET process
primary_theme: bit-column-serial architecture for efficient sparse DNN acceleration
